line: Jung's statements on the six: the number of creation as the conjunction of two and three, the six-rayed mandala, and the six metals under Luna.

sections.title: The six
sections.line: CW9i ¶ 649 and ¶ 664–665: the hexad as a coniunctio, and the mandala with six rays.

quotes.quote: According to old tradition the number 6 means creation and evolution, since it is a coniunctio of 2 and 3 (even and odd = female and male).
The mandala is unusual on account of its six rays, six mountain peaks, six birds, three human figures.
The upper, bright sphere is in the act of descending into the hexad or triad and has already passed the rim of the wheel.

sections.title: The six metals
sections.line: CW14 ¶ 200: Luna as the six planets or spirits of the metals, with Sol the seventh.

quotes.quote: Just as the anima represents and personifies the collective unconscious, so Luna represents the six planets or spirits of the metals.
She is multi-natured, whereas Sol has an exceptional nature as the “seventh from the six spiritual metals.”
